messages.content: I'm interested in environmental science. Does Ramapo have a related major or minor, and are there student organizations where I could meet people with that interest?

expected_behaviors: Search academic programs and student organizations independently.
Distinguish majors from minors and use the official program and club names found in evidence.
Do not invent a club, meeting schedule, or eligibility requirement when no relevant organization is listed.

result.answer:
Yes — Ramapo has both an Environmental Science BS major and an Environmental Science Minor in the School of Theoretical and Applied Science. I also found an Environmental Studies Minor in the School of Social Science and Human Services if you want a related option from a different angle. [Ramapo Programs](https://www.ramapo.edu/majors-minors/environmental-science/) [Ramapo Programs](https://www.ramapo.edu/majors-minors/environmental-studies/)

In the student organization directory, I found Sunrise RCNJ, RCNJ Birding, and Garden Club listed as Student Organizations. I also found Ramapo Green listed there, but it is categorized as a Department rather than a student organization. [Archway Student Organizations](https://archway.ramapo.edu/Sunrise/) [Archway Student Organizations](https://archway.ramapo.edu/Bird/) [Archway Student Organizations](https://archway.ramapo.edu/Garden/) [Archway Student Organizations](https://archway.ramapo.edu/club_signup?view=all&)

The organization records I found only publish names, categories, and website links, not descriptions, so I can’t verify from those records alone which groups are specifically focused on environmental science versus broader nature or sustainability interests. [Archway Student Organizations](https://archway.ramapo.edu/Sunrise/) [Archway Student Organizations](https://archway.ramapo.edu/Bird/) [Archway Student Organizations](https://archway.ramapo.edu/Garden/) [Archway Student Organizations](https://archway.ramapo.edu/club_signup?view=all&)

fields.description: Drop-in for Crystal Queer Tarot, a weekly do-it-yourself space for exploring tarot as a wellness ritual — a creative, mindful way to explore your thoughts and emotions and support mental well-being. Studies show practicing tarot can bring comfort, clarity, and meaning in uncertain times. Whether you are new to tarot or a seasoned reader, this space offers an opportunity to reflect and engage using the cards as tools for self-discovery, self-care, and community building. We’ll have a variety of decks and guidebooks by queer, trans, and women tarotists to inspire your interpretations. From the tarot-curious to the tarot expert, everyone is welcome. Questions or accommodation requests? Please email women@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7468.

fields.title: Quiet Together — Silent Book Club & Silent Space
fields.description: Pause and spend some quiet time in community at the Women’s Center. Quiet Together — Silent Book Club & Silent Space is a weekly evening space to read, study, work, rest, or simply be. From 6–6:30 pm, Silent Book Club participants can settle in, socialize, and share what they’re reading. From 6:30–7:30 pm, the Center becomes a shared quiet space open to everyone, whether you’re participating in Silent Book Club or looking for an hour of peace and quiet. From 7:30–8 pm, participants and Center visitors can optionally talk about their quiet-hour activities. Whether you’re looking for a cozy place to read, a calm space to work, or a chance to decompress, come as you are and enjoy being quietly together. Questions or accommodation requests? Email women@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7468.
